In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the electrical conductivity of thin layers of tantalum pentoxide, Ta 2O 5, of thickness 15 to 250 mμ, deposited on tantalum by thermal evaporation.
the development of a new method of measuring the electrical properties of thin films.
the investigation of the electrical breakdown characteristics of very thin tantalum oxide films.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in the case of the Ta2O5 films, the breakdown voltage is proportional to the film thickness, and is equal to 2,0·106 Volt/cm for films of 250 mμ in thickness, when the Ta metal, on which the film has grown, serves as anode, and mercury in the vacuum as cathode.
the dielectric strength of very thin Ta2O5 films of the range of thickness from 15 to 250 mμ is independent of the thickness of the film and is 2·106 volts/cm.

the electrical breakdown of extremely thin films of Ta2O5 is proportional to the film thickness and that the breakdown field strength for Ta2O5 films up to 250 μ is a constant of 2,0·106 Volt/cm if the tantalum metal on which the film has grown is the anode and the cathode is mercury in a vacuum.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electrical conductivity and the breakdown strength of thin films are not determined by the film thickness but by the film quality.
the breakdown strength of thin Ta2O5 films is not dependent on the film thickness, but on the thickness of the metal substrate.

the breakdown field strength of very thin Ta2O5 films of thickness 15–250 mμ was found to be constant at 2,0·106 volt/cm, when the tantalum, on which the film was grown, is anode and mercury in vacuum is the cathode.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dielectric constant of Ta 2 O 5 is not as high as that of SiO 2, which is the most commonly used gate dielectric material in the semiconductor industry.
the use of a thin Ta2O5 dielectric layer can significantly improve the performance of a Ta2O5-based memristive device.
we have demonstrated that a single layer of Ta2O5 can be used as a high-k dielectric in the fabrication of a high-k MOS capacitor with a low leakage current.
